The eve of Rosh Chodesh, all kinds of... yes.

In any case, however it may be, I do not—I am ashamed to tell everything, and I...

In any case I failed—a descent; I descended a great descent.

And I ate in the morning on this fast day. This, and this weighed upon me, and I had great sorrow.

And I fell into such sadness that it was frightening: whoever looked at me, s... sadness would fall upon him.

Because I had not, had not fasted.

In any case...

And they were all opponents, and they said:

"This is the end of, of Breslov; in the end they go mad."

They thought that this—that I was mad. I had always been in joy.

In any case, I had great sorrow, and also not... and I could not serve Hashem.

I was, I was in darkness, in great sorrow, in such sadness, truly as if going out of one’s mind.

So I prayed to Hashem to have mercy on me and take me out of this.

And that I am causing, I am causing by this a disgrace, a desecration of Hashem for Breslov.

So, so there entered my mind a forceful thought, as if someone were standing and saying words to me:

"Enter your room..."

And there I had a bookcase.

"Open the bookcase and take out some book, whatever book it may be; do not intend any...

Put your hand on a book, take it out, and open it, and open it, yes.

Wherever you open it, there you will find a remedy for your soul."

Nu, so I had such a forceful thought, so I said:

"What, what, what, what can I lose? I will enter the room and I will do it."

Nu, I entered the room, opened the bookcase, took out a book and opened it, and there was...

Oy, is, is, is there something here? Ho, ho, there is something here, yes.

This is the photograph; this is a photograph of the Petek.

I opened the book, and this piece of paper was inside it.

I did not pay attention to the paper.

"Will the paper be a remedy for me? What will a (not understood) paper do for me?"

So I read the halachah where I had opened; perhaps I would find words there that would help me.

So I read, and it revived me, but when I finished, the illness returned as it had been.

Then I lost heart; I thought, Heaven forfend, that I had no...

I had no, no recovery, no hope, no remedy.
